argument_summary: The admissible record does not support clean present-tense compliance on the existing packet, but it does support a narrower position: certification can be defended only as caveated and only if the packet is framed as contingent on pre-launch model-card disclosure of the known small-business onboarding limitation and active monitoring during the 6% reversible rollout. Aggregate readiness passed by 2.1 points, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and rollout controls provide operational containment, but those facts do not by themselves cure the exposed weakness. The overbroad part of the audited claim is any implication that certification is already fully satisfied without confirmed disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is needed to justify the narrower position. The defense rests on risk-weighted governance: readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and the staged reversible rollout supplies bounded operational containment while the disclosed limitation is monitored.
claims_about_policy: The policy standard is narrower than the initial suspicious reading suggests, but it still matters. The admissible evidence shows a material limitation in a named launch use case, an exposed affected segment, and no approved risk acceptance covering that exposure. Under the policy text, rollout controls and monitoring mitigate operational risk but do not remove disclosure duties while the affected segment remains in scope. The supportable position is therefore caveated compliance logic: certification is defendable if treated as conditioned on explicit disclosure before launch, not as unconditional present compliance on the current record.
concessions: The current record does not show an approved risk acceptance that addresses exposure of the small-business onboarding segment.
The current record provided here does not include the final pre-launch model card or equivalent disclosure artifact proving the limitation has already been disclosed.
Rollout percentage, rollback, and monitoring are not sufficient by themselves when the affected use case remains exposed.
